facts.fact: The Adwave article was published on 2025-10-21.
The article's illustrative comparison says a business can spend $600 in two weeks on social media experiments.
facts.quote: You can burn $600 in two weeks of social experiments.

facts.fact: The article's sample starter plan suggests a TV budget of about $50 per month for a small TV footprint run for a full year.
facts.quote: Or you can put about $50 per month toward a small TV footprint for a full year.

facts.fact: Adwave's sample starter plan gives a TV budget of $50 to $150 per month to start, based on market and inventory.
facts.quote: Budget: $50 to $150 per month to start, based on your market and inventory.

facts.fact: Adwave's sample starter plan sets a goal of 5 to 10 exposures per viewer per week in core neighborhoods, repeated for months.
facts.quote: Goal: 5-10 exposures per viewer per week in your core neighborhoods, repeated for months.

facts.fact: Adwave says TV gives 15 or 30 seconds of time on screen to tell a clear story.
facts.quote: Time on screen: 15 or 30 seconds to tell a clear story.

facts.fact: Adwave's starter plan recommends one clean 30 second ad with a single call to action.
facts.quote: Creative: One clean 30 second ad with a single call to action.

facts.fact: The article says a homeowner might be 3 to 6 months from hiring a deck builder.
facts.quote: A homeowner might be 3 to 6 months from hiring a deck builder.

facts.fact: Adwave advises looking for lift in results after the second month of TV advertising.
facts.quote: Look for lift after the second month.

facts.fact: Adwave states that analyzing a website for an ad plan is free, so users can see their plan before spending.
facts.quote: Free to analyze. See your plan before you spend.
